_README: JEOPARDY GAME TEMPLATE — copy this file to make a new game/round
JSON has no real comment syntax, so every underscore-prefixed key
in this file (like this one) is a comment. The server ignores any
field it doesn't recognize, so these are 100% safe to leave in —
delete them once you're comfortable with the format, or don't.
ONE FILE = ONE BOARD:
name        Shown in the host's game picker and on-screen.
categories  The board's columns, left to right. Use 5-6 for a
board that looks right on screen.
clues       Each category's rows, listed CHEAPEST FIRST. Give
every category the same number of clues (5 is
standard) and the same value ladder so the board
lines up into a clean grid.
EACH CLUE HAS THREE FIELDS:
value     Dollar amount. Awarded for a correct buzz, DEDUCTED
for a wrong one. Standard Round-1 ladder: 200/400/
question  The clue text shown big on /display and /play once
selected. (Real Jeopardy phrases this as a statement
and expects an answer phrased as a question — do that
if you like the trivia-night feel, or just write plain
questions. The engine doesn't care either way.)
answer    What the host checks the buzzed-in player against.
Only /host ever receives this field — /display and
/play never get it, even in the raw socket payload,
until the host has marked the clue resolved.
A FULL GAME: ROUND 1 + ROUND 2 ("Double Jeopardy") + FINAL
A real Jeopardy game is three rounds played back to back with score
carried over between them. This engine keeps that simple: each
round is its OWN file in /data, and the host loads them one after
another from the SAME game session. Loading a new file mid-game
only swaps the board/clues — it does NOT reset player scores.
A typical 3-file game looks like:
sample-game.json          Round 1 (this file). Values 200-1000.
sample-game-round2.json   Round 2, "Double Jeopardy". Same shape,
New categories, harder clues.
sample-game-final.json    Final round: ONE category, ONE clue,
no grid. See that file for notes on
what it does (and doesn't) do.
RUNNING A FULL GAME AT THE TABLE:
1. On /host, pick 'Template Game — Round 1' and click Load Game,
then Start Game.
2. Play until every tile on the board is used.
3. Still on /host, pick 'Template Game — Round 2' from the
dropdown and click Load Game again. This swaps in the new
board without touching anyone's score. Keep playing.
4. Repeat for the Final-round file, then click
'End Game / Show Results' once it's answered.
MULTIPLE SEPARATE GAMES (not rounds of the same game):
Any other .json file dropped in /data shows up as its own entry
in the host's picker — e.g. data/movie-night.json,
data/family-trivia.json. Use round-file naming (-round2, -final)
only for files that belong to the same sitting.
name: Template Game — Round 1

categories.name: SCIENCE
categories._note: Category name shows on the board tile — keep it short (one or two words) and it'll fit better on a TV.

clues.question: This gas makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.
This force keeps planets in orbit around the sun.
The chemical symbol Au represents this element.
This scientist developed the theory of general relativity.
This 1997 film about a sinking ship starred Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet.
This studio's mascot is a lamp that hops on the letter 'i'.
This trilogy is set in Middle-earth and based on books by J.R.R. Tolkien.
clues.answer: What is The Lord of the Rings?

clues.question: This director is known for films like Jaws, E.T., and Jurassic Park.
This 1994 film features Andy Dufresne's escape from Shawshank State Penitentiary.

_more_categories_go_here: Copy one of the objects above (name + clues, 5 entries at 200/400/600/800/1000) to add a 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th category. Delete this note and the _README/_note keys whenever you're ready — they're purely documentation.
